scenes.say: Why is it so hard to follow another car closely in Formula One? Blame the dirty air.
A car punches through the air and leaves a swirling wake. The chasing car drives right into it.
The wings and floor get messy airflow and lose downforce. The car slides and the tyres overheat.
Older cars lost almost half their downforce one car length back. The twenty twenty-two cars were meant to lose under a fifth.
So downforce moved under the floor, into tunnels, and the wake behind the car was made narrower.
But teams found loopholes in the wings and brake ducts, and the wake got worse again.
Now the wings move: on the straights the flaps open for everyone, not just the chasing car.
And DRS is gone. Within a second of the car ahead, Overtake Mode gives extra energy for the next lap.
See who's closing in, and by how much, on the LapRadar live map.

title: Dirty air: why it's so hard to follow closely in F1
